definitions.explanation: A book or work written by two or more authors together. Also refers to the act of co-authoring. Common in academic and publishing contexts.

examples.japanese: この{本|ほん}は{二人|ふたり}の{共著|きょうちょ}だ。
examples.english: This book was co-authored by two people.

examples.japanese: {田中|たなか}{先生|せんせい}との{共著|きょうちょ}で{論文|ろんぶん}を{発表|はっぴょう}した。
examples.english: I published a paper co-authored with Professor Tanaka.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{著作|ちょさく}リストには{単著|たんちょ}が{五冊|ごさつ}、{共著|きょうちょ}が{三冊|さんさつ}ある。
examples.english: His list of publications includes five sole-authored works and three co-authored ones.

notes:
USAGE: {共著|きょうちょ} is standard in academic and publishing contexts. In bibliographic references, it often appears after the authors' names, e.g., 「{田中|たなか}・{山田|やまだ}{共著|きょうちょ}」.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {共著|きょうちょ}で{書|か}く: to co-author
- {共著|きょうちょ}{者|しゃ}: co-author
- ～との{共著|きょうちょ}: co-authored with ~

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {共著|きょうちょ}: co-authored work (two or more authors)
- {単著|たんちょ}: sole-authored work
- {編著|へんちょ}: edited and authored work
- {著書|ちょしょ}: authored book (general term)
